J3 aac8 PUSHED. Full suite (re-run clean after the test-helper fix, nothing mutating the tree): 7580 passed / 29 skipped / 114 deselected / 0 FAILED in 29m17s.
Commit: 7 files. GERRIT CHANGE 1013 — https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1013 — stacked on 1011 (J4). Trailers verified, 50/72 hook passed, verify-commit-ticket OK.
STACK: 1009 (J1 MERGED) <- 1010 (J2 green) <- 1011 (J4 green) <- 1013 (J3 pending gates).

=========================================================================
J5 c97f — BLOCKING FACTUAL ERROR FOUND IN THE PLAN. Its plan review PASSED (0 blocking, 1 generic advisory), so this is a defect the LLM reviewer did NOT catch and that I found only by trying to execute it.
=========================================================================
THE CLAIM: J5's Approach says to run 'docker run -dit -p 2990:2990 pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1' and calls it 'a pinned, PULLABLE image carrying its own license'. AC1 says it 'PULLS and starts'.
THE REALITY (verified against primary sources, not assumed):
 * 'docker pull pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1' -> 'pull access denied ... repository does not exist'.
 * Docker Hub API for pycontribs/jira-test-image -> {'message': 'object not found'}. The pycontribs Hub namespace contains exactly 7 repos, all OS base images (centos, fedora, ubuntu, debian, alpine, opensuse, voidlinux). No jira-test-image.
 * The tag is a LOCALLY-BUILT name. pycontribs/jira carries docker/jira-test-image/{Dockerfile,README.md}, and the README's own instruction is 'docker build -t pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1 docker/jira-test-image'. It is published to NO registry.
 * Its base, addono/jira-software-standalone, IS pullable (20k pulls) and the exact digest pycontribs pins (sha256:04326628...) resolves.
So the APPROACH is sound — that image really is the right oracle — but the MECHANISM is wrong: rebar must BUILD it, not pull it.
FEASIBILITY PROVEN BEFORE REMEDIATING (so I do not replace one false premise with another): fetched the upstream Dockerfile, built it here -> 879MB image built OK, container starts and stays up.
THREE LOAD-BEARING DETAILS the plan would otherwise lose, all from the upstream Dockerfile's own comments:
 1. '-DskipAllPrompts=true' is MANDATORY. Atlassian shut down the Marketplace v1 REST endpoint AMPS hardcodes for its SDK update check; without the flag EVERY cold start dies with FileNotFoundException on marketplace.atlassian.com/rest/1.0/plugins/. A maintainer 'tidying' that flag away would break the harness in a way that looks like a network fault.
 2. '-dit' is REQUIRED — AMPS exits without a controlling TTY. A compose service therefore needs tty: true AND stdin_open: true, not a plain service block.
 3. Jira 9+/11+ are UNSUPPORTED on this base (upstream pom anchored to the 8.x dependency graph, fails Maven resolution for newer majors), so JIRA_VERSION is overridable only across 8.x.
PLATFORM CAVEAT I HIT AND MUST RECORD: the base is linux/amd64 and this host is arm64, so it runs under EMULATION. The upstream README says first responsive request is ~3-5 min on native; emulated will be materially slower, so the readiness probe's timeout must be generous and CI runner architecture becomes a real variable for this harness.
DISCIPLINE NOTE: I stopped the emulated Jira container while the J3 full suite ran and restarted it after. This repo has known wall-clock-sensitive tests (see the de-flake commits for the overlap perf gate and test_warm_resolution_is_cheap), and an emulated JVM competing for CPU could have produced a spurious failure — which would have been indistinguishable from a real regression. Startup timing is cheap to re-measure; a poisoned 30-minute suite result is not.
